title: Let’s do something

fn.en: Invite someone and say yes or no politely.
fn.ru: Приглашать и вежливо соглашаться или отказываться.
fn.kk: Шақыру және сыпайы келісу немесе бас тарту.

gr: Let’s · want to · would like to

can.en: I can invite someone and say yes or no politely.
can.ru: Я могу пригласить и вежливо согласиться или отказаться.
can.kk: Шақыра аламын және сыпайы келісіп немесе бас тарта аламын.

tip.en: Let’s + verb · Do you want to + verb · Would you like to + verb.
tip.ru: Let’s + глагол · Do you want to + глагол · Would you like to + глагол.
tip.kk: Let’s + етістік · Do you want to + етістік · Would you like to + етістік.

items.q: ___ go to the cinema this evening!
items.why: Let’s + the plain verb: Let’s go.

items.q: ___ you like to come to the theatre?
I’d like to invite ___ to dinner.
“Do you want to come?” — “___, I can’t. I’m busy.”

items.a: Do you want to join us
Would you like to come with me

lines: Hi Dana! [Let’s|Let’s to|Let us to] do something [this evening|this evenings|in this evening]. 🌆
[Do|Are|Would] you want to go to the cinema with [me|I|my]? 🎬
My brother is free too — [would|do|are] you like to meet [him|he|his]? 👨
“That [sounds|sound|is sound] good! What time?” — “[Let’s|Let’s to|We let] meet at seven.” 🕖
“Sorry, I [can’t|can’t to|don’t can] today. [Maybe|May be|Maybe to] tomorrow?” 🚫

acts.title: Where shall we go?
text: “Where would you like to go?” — “I don’t know. You?” 🤔
“Well, I’d like a drink. There’s a café next to the school.” ☕
“Let’s meet at six. Do you want to invite Marat?” 🕕
“Yes! I want to call him this evening.” 👨📞

items.s: One person would like a drink.
The café is next to the school.
The second person says the idea is bad.
They want to call Marat tomorrow.

items.sit: You want to suggest the cinema to a friend this evening.
o: Let’s go to the cinema this evening.
Let’s to go to the cinema.

items.sit: You and two colleagues are going for lunch. You invite a fourth person.
o: Do you want to join us?
Do you want to join we?

items.sit: You invite your manager to the theatre — this is formal.
o: Would you like to come to the theatre?
Do you want come to the theatre?
You want to come to the theatre?
items.why: With a manager, “Would you like to…?” is the polite form.

items.sit: A friend suggests a coffee and you think it is a great idea.
A friend invites you out, but you have too much work today.
o: Sorry, I can’t. I’m busy today.
Sorry, I don’t can. I’m busy.

items.sit: You ask a colleague to phone Aigul this evening.
o: Can you call her this evening?
Can you call she this evening?
Can you call hers this evening?

lines.s: Good idea. Do you ___ to go to the cinema? 🎬
My brother is free too. Shall we invite ___? 👨
___ you like to meet at seven? 🕖

write.q: Write an invitation and a reply: 5 lines. Use Let’s, Do you want to and one object pronoun. Then say no politely.
write.model: Hi Marat! Let’s do something tomorrow. Do you want to go to the cinema with me? My sister is free too — would you like to meet her? — That sounds good! — Sorry, I can’t tomorrow. I’m busy. Maybe on Saturday?

speak.q: Invite someone out loud in three different ways. Then say yes to one and no politely to another.
speak.model: Let’s go to the cinema this evening. Do you want to join us? Would you like to come with me? — That sounds good! — Sorry, I can’t today. I’m busy.
